whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the CPQ Administrator exam for?

personas.label: Salesforce admins managing CPQ
personas.description: You maintain product catalogs, pricing rules, and quoting workflows in Salesforce CPQ and want the certification to formalize your expertise.

personas.label: Revenue operations professionals
personas.description: You design discount schedules, approval processes, and contract renewal flows and need the credential to validate your quote-to-cash configuration skills.

personas.label: Implementation consultants
personas.description: You configure CPQ bundles, product rules, and price rules for clients and want formal recognition of your ability to deliver CPQ solutions.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the CPQ Administrator Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The CPQ Administrator exam is widely considered one of the harder Salesforce certifications. The ~65% passing score is standard, but the exam covers a dense product with its own data model, pricing waterfall, and rule engine that differ significantly from core Salesforce administration.
bullets: ~65% passing score — standard threshold, but the volume of CPQ-specific concepts (product rules, price rules, discount schedules, bundles) makes achieving it challenging.
CPQ is its own world — the pricing waterfall, Quote Line Editor, and advanced approval framework are unique to CPQ and cannot be learned from general Salesforce admin experience alone.
Scenario-heavy — most questions describe a pricing or quoting requirement and expect you to identify the correct CPQ configuration, not just recall definitions.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Configure a complete quote-to-cash flow in a CPQ developer org — including bundles, product rules, price rules, discount schedules, and at least one approval process — before booking.

examFormat.heading: CPQ Administrator Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Roughly 50-60% of questions are scenario-based. Expect questions describing complex quoting requirements (tiered discounts, bundle constraints, subscription renewals) and asking which CPQ feature or configuration solves the problem.
bestWayToPass: Master Product Rules vs. Price Rules: Know exactly when to use each rule type — product rules control which products appear on a quote, while price rules modify pricing fields on quote lines.
Understand the pricing waterfall: Memorize the CPQ pricing sequence (List → Special → Regular → Customer → Net) and how discount schedules, block pricing, and price rules interact at each stage.
Build bundles hands-on: Create multi-level bundles with features, option constraints, and configuration attributes in a developer org to understand how the Quote Line Editor renders them.
Study the contract lifecycle: Know how contracts generate subscriptions, how renewals auto-create opportunities and quotes, and how amendments handle mid-term product changes with proration.

certificationCard.description: Certified CPQ Administrators are skilled at implementing Salesforce CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) and can expertly design, build, and implement quoting flows.

keyConcepts.h2: CPQ Administrator: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Product Rules vs Price Rules
blocks.body: **Product Rules** control which products appear on a quote — they add, remove, hide, validate, or alert based on product combinations. Types: Alert, Validation, Selection, Filter. **Price Rules** control how products are priced — they evaluate conditions and inject values into quote line fields. The exam frequently tests which rule type applies to a given quoting scenario.

blocks.heading: Bundles and Product Options
blocks.body: A Bundle is a parent product with child Product Options. Options can be required, optional, or pre-selected. Option types control visibility and selectability in the Quote Line Editor. Feature groups organise options within a bundle (e.g., Software, Hardware, Support). Know how option types (Component, Optional, Required, Recommended) affect the configuration experience.

blocks.heading: Discounting: Schedules, Contracted Prices, and Approvals
blocks.body: Discount Schedules apply volume or term-based tiered discounts automatically. Contracted Prices lock negotiated prices for specific products per account, overriding list price on subsequent quotes. Advanced Approvals route discount requests through configurable chains — with threshold-based triggers (e.g., any discount >20% requires manager approval) and automatic approval for within-policy quotes.

blocks.heading: CPQ and the Quote-to-Cash Lifecycle
blocks.body: **CPQ** fits into the Quote-to-Cash process: Opportunity → Quote (built in QLE) → Quote Document (PDF via Quote Template) → Contract (created when Opportunity is Closed Won) → Subscription records (track active products and terms) → Renewal Opportunity (auto-generated at term end). Know which object stores which information at each stage.

blocks.heading: Subscription Products and Renewals
blocks.body: Products can be set as Subscription or One-Time. Subscription products create Subscription records when a Contract is activated. At term end, **CPQ** generates a Renewal Opportunity and Quote populated with existing subscriptions. Amendments create a new Quote from the active Contract to add, remove, or change products mid-term. Understand the difference between Renewal and Amendment flows.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce CPQ Administrator Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The CPQ Administrator exam tests configuration of the full quote-to-cash process using Salesforce CPQ. Scenarios describe complex pricing or quoting requirements — know the CPQ data model and configuration options deeply.

blocks.heading: Product & Bundle Configuration
blocks.body: Know how to configure product options, bundle components, and feature groups. Understand Option Constraints (dependency/exclusion), Nested Bundles, and how Dynamic Bundles adjust products based on field values.

blocks.heading: Pricing Waterfall
blocks.body: Understand the **CPQ** pricing waterfall sequence: List Price → Special Price → Regular Price → Customer Price → Net Price. Know how Discount Schedules, Block Pricing, and **Price Rules** modify prices at each stage.

blocks.heading: Approval Processes in CPQ
blocks.body: **CPQ** **Approval Processes** can trigger based on quote line fields (e.g., discount thresholds). Know how Approval Rules work, how to chain approvals, and how the Approvals object integrates with Salesforce native approvals.

blocks.heading: Quote Document Generation
blocks.body: Know how to configure **Quote Templates** using template content, template sections, and column objects. Understand how DocuSign integration enables e-signature and how quote documents relate to quote lines.

blocks.heading: Contract Amendments & Renewals
blocks.body: Understand how **CPQ** manages contract amendments (adding/removing products mid-term), renewal opportunities (auto-created from contracts), and how co-termination works for multi-asset contracts.

sampleQuestions.question: What does CPQ stand for in Salesforce CPQ?
options: Customer Product Quality
Configure, Price, Quote
Centralized Purchase Queue
Contract Pricing Query
sampleQuestions.explanation: CPQ stands for Configure, Price, Quote - the core capabilities for building and managing product quotes.
whyWrong: 'Customer Product Quality' isn't the actual expansion of CPQ.
'Centralized Purchase Queue' isn't the actual expansion of CPQ.
'Contract Pricing Query' isn't the actual expansion of CPQ.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object is the primary entry point for building a quote in Salesforce CPQ?
options: Opportunity
Quote
Contract
Order
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Quote object is the primary CPQ object used to build, price, and present quotes to customers.
whyWrong: Opportunity is where a quote originates from, but the quote-building itself happens on the Quote object.
Contract is generated after a deal closes, not the entry point for building a quote.
Order is generated after a quote is finalized, not the entry point for building it.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Product Rules in CPQ?
options: To set list prices across all price books
To automatically add, remove, hide, or validate products on a quote based on defined conditions
To assign products to price books and account groups
To track discount approval workflows for the sales manager
sampleQuestions.explanation: Product Rules automatically add, remove, or configure products on a quote based on conditions you define — including Alert, Validation, Selection, and Filter rule types.
whyWrong: Product Rules don't set list prices globally — that's a separate pricing configuration.
Assigning products to price books/account groups is a separate configuration task, not what Product Rules do.
Tracking discount approval workflows is Advanced Approvals' function, not Product Rules'.

sampleQuestions.question: Which CPQ feature applies custom pricing logic to override list prices based on conditions?
options: Price Rules
Product Options
Quote Templates
Discount Schedules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Price Rules evaluate conditions and inject values into quote line fields — enabling dynamic pricing based on customer segment, product combination, quantity, or contract terms.
whyWrong: Product Options define bundle components, not custom pricing override logic.
Quote Templates control document layout, not pricing logic.
Discount Schedules apply tiered discounts but don't provide the broader conditional pricing override logic Price Rules offer.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Bundle in Salesforce CPQ?
options: A report type that groups quote lines by product family
A parent product with optional or required child products (product options) that are configured and priced together
A discount schedule that applies volume-based pricing to a product
A quote template that combines multiple document sections
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Bundle is a product that contains optional or required child products (product options) that can be configured together. Bundles are used for complex product configurations such as hardware + software + services.
whyWrong: A report type groups data for reporting — it isn't a product bundling structure.
A discount schedule applies tiered pricing — it isn't the parent/child bundling structure being described.
A quote template controls document layout — it isn't a product bundling structure.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Discount Schedule in Salesforce CPQ?
options: An approval process that routes large discounts to the sales director for authorisation
A tiered pricing table that automatically applies volume-based or term-based discounts based on quantity ranges
A quote template section that displays discount terms in the PDF output
A Price Rule that overrides list price with a fixed promotional price
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discount Schedules apply tier-based discounts as quantity or term increases — for example, 5% off for 1–10 units, 10% off for 11–50 units. They are associated with a product and applied automatically when the quote meets threshold criteria.
whyWrong: An approval process routes discounts for authorization — that's Advanced Approvals, not a Discount Schedule.
A quote template section displays terms — it doesn't calculate tiered discount pricing itself.
A Price Rule overriding with a fixed price is a different mechanism from the volume/term-based tiering a Discount Schedule provides.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the Salesforce CPQ Quote Line Editor (QLE)?
options: An Apex class that validates quote line totals before a quote is submitted for approval
The interactive grid within the CPQ Quote record where reps configure products, set quantities, apply discounts, and view pricing in real time before generating the document
A Visualforce page used to override the standard Quote PDF template with custom branding
An admin tool for defining the field layout of the Quote object detail page
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Quote Line Editor is the central CPQ workspace for sales reps — it presents products, bundles, quantities, pricing, and discount controls in a grid, and recalculates totals in real time as changes are made.
whyWrong: An Apex validation class is a different technical mechanism, not the interactive UI grid itself.
A Visualforce page for PDF branding is a separate customization, not the QLE.
A field layout admin tool is a separate configuration concern, not the QLE.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Salesforce CPQ handle subscription products at renewal time?
options: Subscription products must be manually re-added to a new quote each renewal period
CPQ automatically generates a Renewal Opportunity and Renewal Quote pre-populated with the subscribed products, quantities, and terms from the original contract
Renewals are managed exclusively in Salesforce Billing and are not a CPQ function
CPQ sends an email notification to the account manager who must manually clone the original quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: When a CPQ Contract is activated, CPQ tracks subscription terms and automatically creates a Renewal Opportunity and Quote at the end of the term — pre-populated with the existing products, enabling seamless renewal management.
whyWrong: Manual re-adding at each renewal is the opposite of CPQ's automated renewal generation.
Renewals are a CPQ function, not exclusively managed in Salesforce Billing.
CPQ automates renewal generation — it doesn't rely on manual email-triggered cloning.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Quote Template in Salesforce CPQ?
options: To define the pricing calculation order for Price Rules on a quote
To control the layout, branding, and sections of the generated CPQ quote PDF document sent to customers
To set default field values when a new Quote record is created from an Opportunity
To define which products are available to a specific sales team based on their profile
sampleQuestions.explanation: Quote Templates define the visual structure of the generated CPQ document — including header/footer, product line columns, terms and conditions, and custom branded sections. Multiple templates can be configured for different markets or product lines.
whyWrong: Quote Templates don't define pricing calculation order — that's a Price Rule concern.
Quote Templates don't set default field values on Quote creation — that's a separate configuration.
Quote Templates don't control product availability by sales team — that's a separate access-control concern.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Advanced Approval in Salesforce CPQ?
options: A standard Salesforce Approval Process adapted to work with CPQ Quote records
A CPQ-native approval framework that supports complex routing — including multi-level approvals, approval chains based on discount thresholds, delegated approvers, and auto-approval rules
An Einstein AI feature that predicts whether a discount will be approved based on historical data
A Quote Template section that displays a signature block for customer approval
sampleQuestions.explanation: CPQ Advanced Approvals provides more sophisticated approval routing than standard Salesforce approvals — supporting threshold-based triggers (e.g., discount > 20%), approval chains, delegated approvers, and automatic approval for within-policy quotes.
whyWrong: A standard Salesforce Approval Process lacks the CPQ-native discount-threshold routing complexity Advanced Approvals provides.
Advanced Approvals isn't an Einstein AI prediction feature — it's a rules-based routing framework.
Advanced Approvals isn't a Quote Template signature section — that's an unrelated document feature.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the relationship between an Opportunity and a CPQ Contract?
options: Contracts are created automatically when an Opportunity reaches the Prospecting stage
After a quote is marked as Primary and the Opportunity is Closed Won, CPQ can generate a Contract from the Opportunity to track subscription terms, renewals, and amendments
CPQ Contracts replace Opportunities in the sales process and are used for all deal tracking
Contracts are only created when Salesforce Billing is installed alongside CPQ
sampleQuestions.explanation: CPQ Contracts are created from Closed Won Opportunities to track active subscriptions. The Contract records the products, quantities, start/end dates, and pricing — forming the basis for renewals and amendments.
whyWrong: Contracts aren't created automatically at Prospecting — that's too early in the sales cycle for a signed agreement.
CPQ Contracts don't replace Opportunities — they track a separate, later-stage agreement concept.
Contracts don't require Salesforce Billing specifically — they're a core CPQ capability on their own.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Lookup Query in Salesforce CPQ Price Rules?
options: A SOQL query written in Apex that retrieves discounts from an external pricing database
A CPQ feature that queries a custom Price Lookup object table to inject a value (such as a discount percentage or price override) into a Price Rule action field based on matching criteria
A Flow element that looks up a related account's contract terms before applying a price
An API call to an external ERP system to retrieve real-time product costs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lookup Queries allow Price Rules to retrieve values from CPQ's custom Price Lookup Tables — enabling complex pricing scenarios such as matrix pricing based on customer tier and product family without custom code.
whyWrong: A Lookup Query isn't Apex/SOQL code — it's a declarative CPQ feature.
A Lookup Query isn't a Flow element — it's a CPQ-native Price Rule mechanism.
A Lookup Query isn't an external API call — it queries an internal custom object table.

sampleQuestions.question: Which CPQ object tracks the products and quantities from a closed-won deal for subscription management?
options: Quote Line Group
Contracted Price
Subscription
Asset
sampleQuestions.explanation: Subscription records are created from CPQ Quote Lines when a Contract is activated — tracking each subscribed product, quantity, pricing, and term dates for ongoing lifecycle management and renewal generation.
whyWrong: Quote Line Group organizes quote lines for display — it isn't the subscription-tracking object.
Contracted Price stores negotiated pricing — it isn't the subscription-tracking object for closed-won deals.
A Quote Line Group doesn't track post-sale subscription data the way an Asset does.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Option Constraint in Salesforce CPQ?
options: A validation rule on the Quote object
A rule that defines dependencies between product options — e.g., Option A required when Option B is selected
A discount approval threshold
A Quote Template section
sampleQuestions.explanation: Option Constraints control the relationship between product options in a bundle — requiring, excluding, or enabling options based on configuration.
whyWrong: A validation rule enforces data entry rules — it isn't the product-option dependency mechanism.
A discount approval threshold routes approvals — it isn't a product dependency mechanism.
A Quote Template section controls document layout — it isn't a product dependency mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: Which CPQ feature allows different pricing for the same product based on customer segment?
options: Quote Templates only
Price Rules with condition-based actions, or Contracted Pricing
Product Rules only
Discount Schedules only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Price Rules and Contracted Pricing allow segment-specific pricing based on account attributes, contract terms, or other criteria.
whyWrong: Quote Templates control document layout, not pricing by customer segment.
Product Rules alone control product visibility/validation, not segment-based pricing.
Discount Schedules alone provide volume tiering, not the broader segment-based Contracted Pricing mechanism.
